security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, static code examples, or normal environment configuration. Confirmed risks are limited to an unsafe 0.0.0.0 development bind, a hardcoded default FastAPI secret, and unpinned dependency installation commands.

remediation.issue: FastAPI template binds to all interfaces by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default the development server to 127.0.0.1 and document when 0.0.0.0 is appropriate for containers.

remediation.issue: FastAPI settings include a reusable placeholder SECRET_KEY default.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the hardcoded default and require SECRET_KEY from environment configuration with startup validation.

remediation.issue: Several setup commands install floating or latest package versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin dependency versions where practical and instruct users to review lockfiles before committing generated projects.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be copied into active repositories without review.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short safety note telling users to run scaffold commands only in a clean workspace after reviewing changes.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Dependency Installation Commands
semantic_findings.description: The scaffold examples use latest or floating dependency installation commands across npm, pip, Go, and npx. Users who run these commands may receive unexpected or compromised upstream packages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly install latest or unpinned packages from package registries. This is a common scaffold pattern, but it creates real supply-chain drift and review risk.

high_findings.title: Generic API/secret keys
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The FastAPI settings example provides a hardcoded default SECRET_KEY value. If users copy the scaffold without replacing it, generated applications may share a predictable signing secret.

medium_findings.title: Hardcoded IP address
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The FastAPI template binds Uvicorn to 0.0.0.0, which can expose a development service beyond localhost. This can be valid in containers, but it is an unsafe default for new scaffolded projects.

content.value_statement: Starting a new project often requires repeated setup across tools, folders, tests, and documentation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured templates for common application stacks.
actual_capabilities: Creates starter structures for React, Express, FastAPI, Go CLI, and Turborepo projects.
Provides example configuration for linting, formatting, testing, TypeScript, and CI workflows.
Outlines directory layouts for frontend, backend, CLI, library, and monorepo projects.
Includes sample package scripts, Makefile targets, requirements files, and workflow steps.
Provides setup checklists and documentation guidance for new repositories.
limitations: Templates are examples and may need updates for the latest framework versions.
The skill does not verify that generated dependencies are safe or still maintained.
Users must replace placeholder secrets and review network exposure before deployment.
It does not implement complete business logic for generated applications.

use_cases.title: Start a Frontend App
use_cases.description: Create a React TypeScript starter with Vite, linting, formatting, tests, and a clear source layout.

use_cases.title: Create an API Foundation
use_cases.description: Generate an Express or FastAPI project structure with routes, middleware, configuration, tests, and documentation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Starters
use_cases.description: Use monorepo and checklist templates to align project setup, CI steps, and developer workflow conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a React App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-scaffolder to create a React TypeScript Vite starter. Include folders, tooling, tests, package scripts, and setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-scaffolder to create a Node.js Express TypeScript API. Include middleware, routes, environment setup, tests, linting, and README sections.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a CLI Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-scaffolder to design a Go CLI project with Cobra, configuration loading, Makefile targets, tests, and release-ready folder structure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Starter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-scaffolder to plan a Turborepo monorepo with apps, shared packages, CI steps, dependency policies, and onboarding documentation.

output_examples.input: Create a React TypeScript application starter for a small product team.
output_examples.output: A Vite React project plan with component folders, test setup, linting, formatting, package scripts, and README guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a FastAPI starter with configuration, tests, and documentation.
output_examples.output: A backend project outline with app modules, environment configuration, dependency files, testing tools, and setup instructions.

output_examples.input: Plan a Turborepo workspace for web, API, and shared packages.
output_examples.output: A monorepo structure with app folders, shared package roles, workflow commands, CI expectations, and setup checklist items.

best_practices: Review generated commands before running them, especially package installation commands.
Replace every placeholder secret, token, and database value before using a scaffolded project.
Pin dependency versions and commit lockfiles when converting examples into production starters.
anti_patterns: Do not run scaffold commands in a repository with uncommitted work unless changes are backed up.
Do not deploy generated templates without replacing local defaults and reviewing exposed ports.
Do not treat generated CI, linting, or security settings as final for every team.

faq.question: What project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers frontend apps, backend APIs, CLI tools, libraries, full-stack projects, and monorepos.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready projects?
faq.answer: It creates strong starter templates, but users must review dependencies, secrets, deployment settings, and team standards.

faq.question: Does it run setup commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides command examples. Users should review commands before execution in their workspace.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes basic environment and tooling guidance, but users must harden generated projects before deployment.

faq.question: Can teams customize the templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can adapt folder structures, scripts, CI steps, and dependency choices to match internal standards.
